newsitem.title: FRANCE: Guinness, GrandMet say LVMH has made new proposals.
newsitem.headline: Guinness, GrandMet say LVMH has made new proposals.

text.p: British companies Guinness Plc and GrandMet said on Tuesday that French conglomerate LVMH had made new proposals during talks last week and on Tuesday in London.

The proposals "did not involve the wholesale demerger of the companies' non-spirits and wine activities, but contemplated the break-up of Moet Hennessy with the champagne business becoming wholly-owned by LVMH and the cognac business being acquired for shares in (Guinness unit) UDV," a statement received in Paris said.
They said they would study the proposals when they had further details.

"While there were elements of the new outline proposals which would not be in the best interests of GrandMet's and Guinness' shareholders in the form proposed, GrandMet and Guinness will assess in full the commercial and financial logic of this new proposal when it is detailed in writing," the statement said.

"...it is too early to say whether there any agreement can be reached," it said, adding that any proposal would be judged against the benchmark of value for shareholders and the fair distribution of such value among all the shareholders involved.

Earlier on Tuesday, an LVMH spokewoman said the French group was still working on the hypothesis of a three-way marriage between the three companies, following newspaper reports that said LVMH could swap its cognac for champagne with Guinness.
LVMH has said it was opposed to a merger between Guinness and GrandMet.
